display: Birth doula in training (DONA pathway) in South Manchester, setting up my own practice and taking my first clients.

signals.text: I'm looking for a local midwife, or someone who knows how Greater Manchester maternity services work, who would answer my practical questions occasionally.
I need a plain-English way to find out my local hospitals' policies on water birth and on induction, and how the Maternity Voices Partnership works.
I'm still setting up my practice and need to sort out doula insurance as a sole trader.
I keep going round in circles on where 'sharing what the NICE guideline says' ends and 'giving medical advice' begins, and I'd like to talk it through with someone experienced.
Clients are asking me clinical-sounding questions I can't answer yet, and I freeze. I don't want to say more than 'it's your decision'.
I'm worn out. My toddler started nursery and keeps catching colds, so I'm up at night while I revise for my course.
I have no practice income yet, and the bathroom and nursery fees are running. Money is tight.
I'm at the point where I need a few more paying clients, or at least people who could refer them. I have two so far.
My Instagram only has 87 followers. People who find it often don't understand what a doula does, and my replies feel too small.
The family bathroom renovation is stuck. We're washing in the sink until the tiler comes on the 20th, and the budget is £2,800.
I have to log case hours and finish modules 5 and 6 before I can be on call, and I'm behind.
My course buddy and I have the same worries about clinical scope, and we're both wishing for a midwife friend.
I worry that I'm not qualified enough and that clients will find out. It's harder in weeks when I can't answer their questions.
My own first birth involved an induction, an emergency section and no one explaining what was happening. Working through it is why I'm doing this.

offers.text: Birth doula support in South Manchester: antenatal visits, being with you at the birth, and a postnatal visit. The package is £600.
Help for expectant parents to prepare questions and a birth preferences plan, and to ask what is happening and what their options are.
A birth bag I bring to births: birthing ball, TENS machine, massage oils, rebozo and laminated position cards.
Eight years of working with young children and their parents in a primary school. I stay patient and calm when the room is tense.
Clear, friendly writing for parent-facing material, such as posts or short guides about birth positions and what a doula does.
Warm introductions within my local network of two independent midwives in Chorlton, a hypnobirthing teacher and a postnatal physio.
A listening ear for parents who had a frightening or unexplained birth and want to be heard.
I can drive and go to people's homes in South Manchester, with set time on Tuesdays when my mum has my toddler.
I'm a peer for other trainee doulas on case logs, reading lists and sharing what we learn.

catchers.hypo: I'm a midwife or ex-midwife in Greater Manchester. I'd like to help new doulas understand what's in the guidelines and where a doula's role stops. Do you know anyone who'd want that?
catchers.can: I'd be glad of this. It's what I most need right now, and I can offer something back: referrals, local connections, or help writing it up.
catchers.confirm: Are you able to talk to trainee doulas about local maternity pathways and guideline basics, without giving advice about individual cases?

catchers.hypo: I'm expecting in South Manchester and have never heard of a doula. I'd like to understand what you do and how that's different from my midwife.
catchers.can: I can explain what a doula does and what she doesn't. I can offer a free first conversation and, if it fits, antenatal, birth and postnatal support.
catchers.confirm: Are you pregnant (or supporting someone who is), living in or around South Manchester, and due after December?

catchers.hypo: I'm a trainee doula in another city. I'm stuck on the case log and what I'm allowed to say to clients. Could we compare notes?
catchers.can: I can swap notes, share reading lists and case-log tips, and keep each other going. My course buddy in Leeds could join too.
catchers.confirm: Are you on, or about to start, a DONA-type doula course and willing to swap experience without sharing any client's identity?

catchers.hypo: I work with a software company and need someone to test a pregnancy or birth-planning app with careful attention to detail and real users in mind.
catchers.can: I can't do this myself, but my husband is a professional software tester. I can introduce you, and I can give feedback as a doula on the content.
catchers.confirm: Is this a paid testing job that needs a professional software tester?

catchers.hypo: I'm a retired school secretary looking for ways to help in a community. Do you know anyone who can use admin help?
catchers.can: My mum in Stockport is a retired school secretary. If the work fits her, I can introduce her, since she's already helping me with childcare and paperwork.
catchers.confirm: Is this a small voluntary or low-pressure admin job in or near Stockport?

catchers.hypo: I run a local pregnancy group or antenatal class in Manchester. Would you come and talk to our parents about what a doula does?
catchers.can: I can give a short talk or a Q&A on a doula's role, birth positions and getting your questions answered at a birth.
catchers.confirm: Is this a group of expectant parents in Greater Manchester, with a talk of about 30–60 minutes that doesn't require me to give medical advice?

catchers.hypo: I'm a sole-trader doula in the UK. I found a decent insurer, or a good way to get cover. Does anyone need it?
catchers.can: I do need insurance. I'd like names, prices and what to check for, and I can pass on what I learn.
catchers.confirm: Is this insurance for UK sole-trader birth doulas, rather than for midwives or general business cover?

catchers.hypo: I had a birth that left me confused or upset. I just want to talk to someone who won't say 'at least the baby is healthy'.
catchers.can: I can listen and help you work out which questions to ask your hospital or your midwife. I can't offer therapy or tell you what went wrong medically.
catchers.confirm: Do you want to talk through the experience and think about next steps, rather than get a clinical review of what happened?

catchers.hypo: I'm a tiler or plumber in south Manchester and can take on a small bathroom job at a fair price. Do you know anyone?
catchers.can: I have a bathroom renovation on a tight budget. It's a real job, with tiling on the 20th and plumbing still being sorted.
catchers.confirm: Do you work in or near Manchester, and can you take on a small domestic job at a fixed or capped price?

forbids.text: I will not give medical advice or diagnose. I only help people find information and decide for themselves.
I can't be on call for births until module 6 is signed off.
Childcare is only on Tuesdays, and I must be home by 6.
I won't share any client's identity or medical details with anyone.
I won't promise outcomes or recommend avoiding medical care.
I can't take on work that needs me to travel far or be away overnight right now.

projects.name: Whitlow Doula (practice setup)
projects.text: Setting up a sole-trader birth doula practice in South Manchester. I have a logo, a one-page contract, a £600 package and two clients. Insurance is still to do.
roles_needed: referrers such as midwives, hypnobirthing teachers, physios
someone to help with the website or Instagram

projects.name: Family bathroom renovation
projects.text: A low-budget bathroom redo with about £2,800. The wallpaper is stripped, the tiler comes on the 20th, and plumbing and fittings are still open.
roles_needed: someone to share tips on cheap fittings

policy.t1: If there's a real sign of collaboration, I'll share the kinds of questions clients ask that I can't yet answer, and my worries about where doula support stops and medical advice starts. I'll also introduce my local midwives, physio and hypnobirthing teacher.
policy.t2: Once trust is clear and I know who I'm talking to, I'll share my own birth experience and my worry about not being qualified enough.
policy.never: Clients' identities, medical details, or anything that could identify them.
